;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[History of the Syrian Civil War (2020–present)]]
***[[Al-Bab truck bombing]]
****A [[truck bomb]]ing kills at least 18 people and injures another 75 in [[al-Bab]], [[Aleppo Governorate]], [[Syria]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/10/6/at-least-11-dead-in-blast-in-northwest-syrian-town-of-al-bab (Al Jazeera English)]
*[[2020 Kyrgyzstani protests]]
**Protesters in [[Kyrgyzstan]] break into [[Supreme Council (Kyrgyzstan)|parliament]] in the capital [[Bishkek]], throwing paper from windows and [[arson|setting the building on fire]]. A person is killed and 686 others are injured. [https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSKBN26R05T (Reuters)]
**The electoral authorities in Kyrgyzstan annul the results of the [[2020 Kyrgyz parliamentary election|parliamentary elections]] following the protests. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-54432030 (BBC News)]
**Opposition groups claim to be in power after seizing [[government of Kyrgyzstan|government]] buildings in the capital. [[President of Kyrgyzstan|President]] [[Sooronbay Jeenbekov]] says he is facing a [[coup d'état]]. Several provincial governors reportedly resign. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-kyrgyzstan-protests/opposition-in-kyrgyzstan-claim-power-after-storming-government-buildings-idUSKBN26R05T?il=0 (Reuters)]
**[[Prime Minister of Kyrgyzstan|Prime Minister]] [[Kubatbek Boronov]], who is a close ally of the ruling President, resigns. He is replaced by [[Sadyr Japarov]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/kyrgyzstan-prime-minister-kubatbek-boronov-resigns-reports-claim/a-55178024 (DW)]
*[[Second Nagorno-Karabakh War]]
**[[Azerbaijan]] accuses the [[Armed Forces of Armenia|Armenian Armed Forces]] of attacking the [[Baku–Tbilisi–Ceyhan pipeline]] with banned [[cluster munition]]s, killing a civilian in [[Goranboy District]]. [[Armenia]] rejects the accusation. [https://www.rferl.org/a/azerbaijan-says-pipeline-targeted-in-fighting-armenia-rejects-accusation/30879737.html (RFE/RL)]
*[[Mali War]]
**[[Jihadist]] group [[Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal Muslimin]] releases [[Mali]]an opposition leader [[Soumaïla Cissé]], who had been held captive since March, and French aid worker Sophie Pétronin, who had been held captive since 2016. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/oct/06/kidnapped-mali-politician-and-french-aid-worker-freed (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Papua conflict]]
**Members of the [[Free Papua Movement]] fire five bullets at the Indonesian Army security post in Pasar Baru Kenyam, [[Nduga Regency|Nduga]] district, [[Papua (province)|Papua]]. A civilian is injured. [https://en.antaranews.com/news/158345/armed-papuan-group-shoots-civilian-in-nduga-district (Antara)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Hurricane Delta]]
**Hurricane Delta strengthens into a powerful [[Category 4 hurricane]], with additional strengthening anticipated until landfall in [[Quintana Roo]], Mexico. [https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/text/refresh/MIATCUAT1+shtml/061520.shtml? (National Hurricane Center)]
**Governor of [[Louisiana]] [[John Bel Edwards]] declares a [[state of emergency]] ahead of the storm. [https://www.wdsu.com/article/gov-edwards-declares-state-of-emergency-ahead-of-hurricane-delta/34290778 (WDSU-TV)]
*The death toll of the floods brought on by the [[2020–21 European windstorm season]], which is affecting France and Italy rise to 14 as the body of a worker is found in the Italian region of [[Liguria]]. The man went missing during the beginning of the floods three days ago. [https://www.tgcom24.mediaset.it/cronaca/liguria/maltempo-liguria-tra-otto-cadaveri-recuperati-anche-operaio_23836180-202002a.shtml (TGCOM24)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.]]
****[[White House COVID-19 outbreak]]
*****[[White House]] [[Senior Advisor to the President of the United States|senior policy adviser]] [[Stephen_Miller_(political_advisor)|Stephen Miller]] tests positive for COVID-19. [https://amp.cnn.com/cnn/2020/10/06/politics/stephen-miller-tests-positive-coronavirus/index.html (CNN)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)]]
****[[New York (state)|New York state]] will reinstate restrictions on businesses, houses of worship and schools in and near areas where coronavirus cases are spiking, governor [[Andrew Cuomo]] said. The new rules will affect parts of [[Brooklyn]] and [[Queens]] in New York City, sections of Orange and Rockland counties in the [[Hudson Valley]], and an area within Binghamton in the Southern Tier. This restrictions will take effect no later than Friday. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/schools-closed-virus-hot-spots-nyc-battles-flare-73451226 (ABC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****The number of daily cases in [[Malaysia]] reaches 691, a record for two consecutive days. The [[Ministry of Health (Malaysia)|Health Ministry]]'s director-general [[Noor Hisham Abdullah]] says that of those new cases, 397 of them were from [[Kedah]], with most of them being caused by an outbreak in a prison. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/malaysia-reports-691-new-covid-19-cases-record-high-for-second-consecutive-day (''The Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates]]
****The [[United Arab Emirates]] surpasses 100,000 [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] cases. In addition, six people have died in the past 24 hours, the highest single day figure since May. [https://amp.thenational.ae/uae/health/uae-records-1-061-new-cases-as-it-passes-100-000-mark-1.1089276 (''The National'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Andorra]]
****The Andorran [[Prime Minister of Andorra|Prime Minister]] [[Xavier Espot]] self-isolates for 10 days after having a close contact with a positive for COVID-19. [https://www.diariandorra.ad/noticies/nacional/2020/10/06/espot_confina_per_ser_contacte_positiu_167899_1125.html (''Diari d'Andorra'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Finland]]
****[[Finland]] reports its highest daily number of COVID-19 cases since the start of the [[COVID-19 pandemic|pandemic]], with 227 new cases reported, surpassing the previous peak in April. They also exceed the rate that the country has set for other countries before their citizens are allowed to visit without being [[quarantine]]d. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-finland-cases-idUSKBN26R210 (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland]]
****[[Poland]] reports 58 new deaths, a record high for a single day since the beginning of the [[pandemic]]. [https://thehill.com/policy/international/europe/519778-poland-reports-record-number-of-covid-19-deaths (''The Hill'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vatican City]]
****The Secretary General of the Governorate of Vatican City State announces that as of 7 October it will also be mandatory to wear masks outdoors when it is not possible to maintain a safety distance. This rule will also apply in the extraterritorial properties of the Vatican in the city of Rome. [https://www.catholicnewsagency.com/news/vatican-city-state-makes-masks-compulsory-outdoors-84199 (Catholic News Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***The [[European Medicines Agency]] announces that they will launch a review for [[vaccine]]s developed by [[Pfizer]] and [[BioNTech]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/10/06/eu-launches-rolling-review-of-pfizer-biontech-coronavirus-vaccine.html (CNBC)]

;International relations
*[[Indonesia–Philippines relations]]
**[[Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries (Indonesia)|Indonesian Minister of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries]] [[Edhy Prabowo]] says that they have detained two [[Philippines|Filipino]] [[fishing boats]] with 21 crew members on board, in [[Exclusive economic zone of Indonesia|Indonesia's Exclusive Economic Zone]]. [https://en.antaranews.com/news/158333/indonesia-detains-two-filipino-fishing-boats (Antara)]

;Law and crime
*The [[European Court of Justice]] rules that [[Prime Minister of Hungary|Hungarian Prime Minister]] [[Viktor Orbán]]'s [[higher education]] reforms violate the [[Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union|EU Charter of Fundamental Rights]], saying they placed undue burdens on foreign universities operating in the country. [[Philanthropist]] [[George Soros]], whose [[Central European University]] was targeted by Orbán's laws, laments that "the decision [came] too late" and that the university will not return after being forced out because "[Hungary's] prevailing laws don’t meet the requirements of academic freedom". [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/eu-court-rules-hungarys-orban-soros-university-73446045 (ABC News)]

;Science and technology
*[[Nobel Prize in Physics]]
**The [[Nobel Prize in Physics]] is awarded to [[Roger Penrose]] "for the discovery that black hole formation is a robust prediction of the general theory of relativity," and to [[Reinhard Genzel]] and [[Andrea M. Ghez]] "for the discovery of a supermassive compact object at the centre of our galaxy." [https://www.cbc.ca/news/technology/nobel-prize-physics-2020-1.5751726 (CBC)]
*[[Mars]] makes its closest approach to Earth since 2018. Mars will not be closer to Earth again until 2035. [https://www.space.com/mars-closest-to-earth-until-2035 (Space.com)]

***The [[NHL entry draft]], originally postponed due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, is held remotely with the [[New York Rangers]] selecting [[Winger (ice hockey)|winger]] [[Alexis Lafrenière]] with the [[List of first overall NHL draft picks|first overall pick]].
